title: Barriers to Deploying Solar Panels in New Buildings, and Private Residential and Commercial Spaces
what_it_is: Barriers to Deploying Solar Panels in New Buildings, and Private Residential and Commercial Spaces

sections.label: Solar panels private buildings barriers
sections.summary: Asks about barriers to solar deployment in private residential and commercial spaces and whether more measures are considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what has the Ministry assessed to be the key barriers to deploy solar panels in private residential and commercial spaces, including spaces managed by Management Corporations Strata Titles; and (b) whether additional measures, such as grants, financing support, property tax reliefs or regulatory adjustments, are being considered to address these barriers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We have achieved two gigawatt-peak of installed solar capacity island-wide and have set an increased target of three gigawatt-peak by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: For private residential buildings, the number with solar panels has increased more than four times in the last five years, from around 1,400 in 2020 to around 6,900 in 2025.

sections.label: Grant support building owners
sections.summary: Eligible building owners can get grant support up to 50% of energy improvement costs, capped at $1.2 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Depending on the overall carbon abatement achieved, eligible building owners can benefit from grant support of up to 50% of the cost of their energy improvement works, capped at $1.2 million.

sections.label: New buildings environmental code solar
sections.summary: New buildings must meet BCA Code standards, with solar recognised as an acceptable carbon-reduction measure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: New buildings are required to meet standards under the Building and Construction Authority's (BCA's) Code for Environmental Sustainability of Buildings, with solar being recognised as one of the acceptable carbon-reduction measures under the Code.

sections.label: Fire safety solar panel exemptions
sections.summary: Simplified fire safety requirements exempt over half of solar installations on metal-roofed buildings, saving up to 30% on construction costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The simplified fire safety requirements exempt more than half of all solar panel installations on metal-roofed buildings, and this basically allows eligible business owners to save up to 30% on total construction costs.

sections.label: Solar training and MCST approvals
sections.summary: SkillsFuture partners Sembcorp Solar to train workers, and MCST approval threshold may be reduced from 75% to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Specifically, for solar, SkillsFuture Singapore also partners Sembcorp Solar as a SkillsFuture Queen Bee since 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: This is to uplift other companies in this sector in training their workers and for us to be able to generate that talent pipeline that is needed to sustain this ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I received feedback from private property owners and Management Corporations Strata Title (MCSTs) on concerns and uncertainties with regard to procurement, financing structures and even things like warrantees on waterproofing, reliability and maintenance, something which the Minister of State alluded to earlier; and in the case of MCST, the high threshold for approvals to adopt solar energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, hence, I would like to ask the Minister of State, will the Ministry first assist to streamline the MCST approval process so that we can drive and accelerate solar adoption on private property, such as condominiums?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This will all drive a wider adoption and accelerate solar adoption in private properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: They are exploring a reduction from 75% to possibly 50%.
